history: Il voto is a small word that you meet at the school, at the polling station and in church. Its source is Latin votum, a vow made to the gods, from vovere, ‘to promise solemnly’. A voto first meant a wish or promise, as it still does when a monk or nun takes i voti. From the idea of a wish expressed to an authority came the idea of an opinion expressed in an assembly: andare a votare. In school the teacher expresses a judgement of your work as a number, so un bel voto is a good grade, and ten is the highest. In the Catholic tradition an ex voto is an object left in a church to thank for a granted wish. English vote and vow come from the same Latin source.
